issue: The OVERFLOW_EPISODES row's 2026-10-06 note says "a window lasts at most `OVERFLOW_PROBE_DEFERRAL_CAP_SECS` (380 s)". The scope-lock stub says the same with no qualifier ("so a window lasts at most 380 s"). The plan ITEM 51 says "the window lasts at most 380 s after its first frame (Verified by proptest_attribution_rules)". In the code the cap is measured from `first_frame_at`, and `watched_went_down` (the probed socket's first coded close, or a teardown we start on a failed subscribe or main-feed silence) resets `first_frame_at = None` and `phase_since = now`. So the 380 s clock starts over after a restart. The time before the first frame (up to `OVERFLOW_PROBE_FIRST_FRAME_DEADLINE_SECS`, 120 s, once per dial) is outside the cap, and `past_note_cutoff` returns false while `first_frame_at` is None, so siblings are noted with no cutoff in that phase. The proptest only checks `now - ep.first_frame_at < cap` against the CURRENT first frame, so it does not verify the published bound. Verified by reading `poll`, `watched_went_down`, `past_note_cutoff` and the proptest assertion near line 20576.
scenario: After an 805 the main feed grants a probe at t=0. The first frame arrives at t=119. A sibling drops and is noted, keeping the pass deferred. At first frame + 379 s (t=498) the probed socket gets an 807 and its watch restarts. Its new first frame arrives at t=617, and a new deferral can run to 617 + 380 = t=997. The window is held for about 16.6 minutes, not 380 s. During all of it `holds_turn()` is true, so the depth episode cannot grant any parked depth socket. An operator or reviewer who trusts the 380 s figure (stated as Verified) gets the depth recovery delay wrong by about 2.6x, and nothing tests the true bound.
fix: Correct the claim in CLAUDE.md, the scope-lock stub, the full scope-lock 'Pass deferral' row and plan ITEM 51 to the true bound. That is 380 s after the probed socket's latest first frame; from the grant, up to 120 s to the first frame plus at most one restart (adding up to 120 s plus the time already spent) plus 380 s, about 1,000 s worst case. Alternatively, enforce an absolute bound from the grant: keep the original grant instant in a field that `watched_went_down` does not reset, and fail with `FailedDeferralExhausted` once it is exceeded. Either way, add a proptest assertion that checks the stated bound against the grant instant (or the first-ever first frame), not the reset `first_frame_at`.

issue: A dial that FAILED still counts as a possible eviction. The dial-start stamp (OVERFLOW_DIAL_BEGIN_MS) is written at BeginDial and is never cleared when the dial fails. Dhan evicts the oldest socket only when it ACCEPTS a new one, and a dial refused at the upgrade (HTTP 400/401/429) accepts nothing, yet its stamp still counts as corroboration for 20 s. One socket stuck in a failing-dial loop re-stamps itself on every attempt, about every 30-45 s at the ladder cap. With such a loop running, most unrelated sibling blips land within 20 s of a fresh stamp, so the window fails with failed_eviction_corroborated. That is the old burn-a-probe-per-blip behaviour this PR exists to remove. The rule file's 'any of our sockets beginning a dial within 20 s' limit describes a coincidence, not a loop that makes the rule fire almost every time. No test covers a DialFailed loop.
scenario: An 805 has engaged the episodes and a main-feed probe window is running on slot 2. Depth-20 slot 7 is in a DialFailed loop: HTTP 400 on every upgrade (the 2026-08-12 blackout pattern), or a 429 storm. Each retry runs BeginDial, which calls overflow_note_dial_begin(7). At F+60 main-feed slot 0 drops with no code for an unrelated reason. Slot 7 stamped 12 s earlier, so recent_dials holds bit 7. Bit 7 is neither the closer nor in the burst, so evictors != 0 and the window gives FailedEvictionCorroborated. The probe is spent, and after three such blips the main feed is DownForSession, although slot 7 never opened a connection and so could not have evicted anyone.
fix: In the DialFailed arm, clear the slot's stamp when the failure proves the server did not accept the socket (an upgrade response other than 101, using the reason socket.last_dial_failure_reason() already reports): one Release store of 0 into OVERFLOW_DIAL_BEGIN_MS[slot]. Keep the stamp on a timeout, where acceptance is unknown, because there it errs toward fail as intended. Add a test: a stamped slot whose dial is rejected does not corroborate a sibling's close 5 s later; a timed-out dial still does. Record the remaining limit (timeouts still count) in the 2026-10-06 scope-lock section.
